children: Amazon and Boeing stocks were both pointing lower Tuesday as the investigation into a fatal plane crash at Miami International Airport ramped up.

Five people died after an Amazon Boeing 767 cargo plane, operated by all-cargo airline 21 Air, overshot the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday. Two crew members were on board-the pilot and co-pilot-and the plane was completing its third flight of the day as it landed just before 2 p.m. Eastern time.

But the plane failed to stop, striking navigation devices, a white Ford Econoline van with seven people inside, a fence, and a Toyota Corolla Cross car, National Transportation Safety Board (NSTB) chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said Monday. It then hit another fence before coming to a stop in a Tesla robo-taxi station.
The 32-year-old Boeing plane flew commercial flights from the time it was built in 1994 until 2015, when it was converted into a cargo plane, according to flight-tracker Flightradar 24.

The NSTB has deployed a team of 32 investigators, who will be in Miami for at least a week. They will split into smaller teams to investigate several areas including operations and human performance, aircraft performance, airplane systems, engines, weather, and runway design and emergency response.

The operations team will examine 21 Air's policies and its contract with Amazon. "It's Amazon's operation for cargo but Amazon contracted with 21 Air," Homendy told reporters. "Who does what with safety provisions?"
Amazon did not immediately respond to a Barron's request for comment early Tuesday.
The company said just 3% of its transoceanic shipments traveled by air in 2025, down from 10% in 2024, in its sustainability report released in July.

21 Air is an all-cargo airline with its headquarters in Greensboro, North Carolina, according to its currently inaccessible website. The airline has a 24/7 operations center in Miami, where pilot and loadmaster crew teams are stationed.

The carrier is authorized for interstate and foreign air transportation of property and mail operating Boeing 767 all-cargo aircraft, and authorized to operate cargo services between the U.S. and Mexico, its website added. 21 Air did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Boeing said it was supporting the NTSB investigation, in an emailed statement to Barron's.
Amazon shares were down 0.7%, while Boeing slipped 0.6% as S&P 500 futures pointed 0.2% lower ahead of the open.
